frontier.hypothesis: A PERM_* directed macro (per .claude/rules/permuter-directives.md) targeting specifically the if/else clamp's temp-variable structure (e.g. sweeping whether the masked value is bound to a named local vs. used inline, or the branch-sense of the if/else) may reach the a0-homing that plain random mutation did not find in ~26k iterations.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c/global.c allocno priority for a parameter-homed pseudo vs. a freshly computed one; directed mutation narrows the search to exactly the C-structure axis that affects this tiebreak instead of exploring the whole function.
frontier.next_probe: Use tools/permuter_annotate.py (or hand-annotate) the clamp region in tmp/grind/_SsVmInit/s5/perm_ws/base.c with PERM_GENERAL alternatives for the if/else body and temp binding, then re-launch a short directed campaign against the now-working workspace.

frontier.hypothesis: Hand-deriving GCC 2.7.2's find_reg/allocno-priority computation directly from local-alloc.c for this exact case (a value that both originates as a live parameter register AND is the sole live value at the branch) may show which C-level spelling change makes local-alloc prefer a0 over the first-free v0, without needing the permuter at all.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c's REG_LIVE_LENGTH / regno-preferencing (reg_preferred_or_nothing / basic-block-local allocation) for a pseudo whose live range starts at a hard-reg-homed parameter.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/local-alloc.c's block_alloc / find_reg and the preference-computation around REGNO(parameter) for a pseudo consumed once immediately after; identify whether a specific block-local liveness shape (e.g. avoiding the extra sltiu-only use of s1 elsewhere) would flip the allocation to a0.
